## Summary

The analysis agent can now run from a run YAML ("run it from config `<run.yaml>`") as well as from the interactive questions. Both front ends produce the same config in the schema of the perf report wrapper from #1094, and a new `config_utils` module completes and checks it in Step 0. Step 1 is then one `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config` call instead of per-mode CLI command lines that the orchestrator assembled from prose.

**Depends on #1094.** This branch carries its three commits (`de5daaec..c3e838a8`); review from `c3e838a8`. The changes here are commits `23a05ff7`, `dfa914b7` and `9c397e96`.

## Why

| Pain point | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-node support | Inputs came from Step 0 questions and hand-built command lines, sized for one or two traces | A run config with a `jobs` list is the input a multi-node run needs. This PR lays that groundwork; the scopes still take one or two jobs |
| Step 1 assembled in prose | `reference.md` branched on analysis mode and comparison scope, with per-CLI flag suffix tables for `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch` and `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch_inference`; the LLM built each command line | One wrapper call on `cache/run_config.yaml` |
| Interactive only | Every run went through the Step 0 questions | YAML mode: the prompt names a config file and the agent asks only the environment questions |
| Wiring left to the LLM | Job names, the comparison target and the agent's required report flags came from prose instructions | `check_config` adds them in code and prints every change |
| Late, one-at-a-time errors | Scope rules (one job vs two, capture folder on both or neither, semantic is inference only) were prose checks | All shape errors are raised together in Step 0, then the wrapper's own validation runs before anything is generated |
| No record of the run | The inputs lived only in the conversation | `cache/run_config.yaml` (agent input) and `run_config.resolved.yaml` (every flag explicit, written by the wrapper) |

## Architecture

### Step 0: two front ends, one config

```
Interactive mode                                 YAML mode
Step 0 answers (scope, mode, trace(s),           user run.yaml
platform(s), capture folder, extension)          ("run it from config <run.yaml>")
        │                                                │
        ▼                                                ▼
config_utils build                               config_utils check
  --scope --analysis_mode --output_dir             --config <run.yaml> [--scope]
  --job k=v,... (per job)  --set k=v               load_run_config()
  _assign_pairs()                                        │
        └──────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
              check_config(config, scope) -> AnalysisConfig
                1. shape: platform per job, absolute paths,
                   _shape_errors(scope)          ── ConfigError (all errors at once)
                2. complete:
                     standalone   drop jobs[0].name
                     two jobs     names trace1/trace2, jobs[1].platform := jobs[0]'s
                                  (original kept as platform2)
                     comparative  jobs[0].compare_to := jobs[1] paths
                     all          AGENT_REPORT_FLAGS[analysis_mode]
                3. wrapper: plan_reports(completed)  ── ConfigError
                               │
                ┌──────────────┴──────────────────┐
                ▼                                 ▼
  <output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml     stdout: change lines (added/set/renamed/removed)
  (Step 1 input)                                 then key=value variables:
                                                 comparison_scope, trace_path, platform,
                                                 output_dir [, comparison_method,
                                                 trace2_path, platform2]  ──► Steps 1-12
```

Scopes map to the wrapper schema as follows. `semantic` is the comparative graph-replay-only case.

| Scope | Jobs | `compare_to` | `capture_folder` | `comparison_method` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| standalone | 1 | none | optional | n/a |
| comparative | 2 | added to job 1 | both jobs or neither | tracediff |
| semantic | 2, inference only | none | none | semantic |

### Step 1: pre-processing, then one wrapper call

```
cache/run_config.yaml
        │
        ├── comparison_method = semantic only ─────────────────────────────┐
        │                                                                  ▼
        │                          semantic-comparison sub-agent
        │                            ─► semantic/tracediff_output/diff_stats.csv
        │                          config_utils set-diff-stats --config ... --path ...
        │                            add_diff_stats(): jobs[0].precomputed_diff_stats
        │                                                                  │
        ◄──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        ▼
TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config --config <output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml
        │  writes run_config.resolved.yaml, then runs each job in order
        │  non-zero exit or timeout ─► [DIAG:pipeline:STEP1_FAIL], stop
        ▼
perf_report.xlsx + perf_report_csvs/                     (standalone)
perf_report_trace1.xlsx/_csvs/ + perf_report_trace2.xlsx/_csvs/   (two jobs)
        │
        ▼
Step 2 trace-quality gate (skipped when comparison_method = semantic)
        │
        ▼
Steps 3-12 unchanged
```

## What changed

### Python (2 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `TraceLens/Agent/Analysis/utils/config_utils.py` | New. `check_config`, `add_diff_stats`, `AnalysisConfig`, and the `build` / `check` / `set-diff-stats` CLI. Imports `ConfigError`, `load_run_config` and `plan_reports` from the wrapper and leaves the wrapper unchanged |
| `TraceLens/Agent/Analysis/evals/eval_utils/workflow_scripted_evals.py` | Step 1 remediation text names `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config` |

### Orchestrator skill (2 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `skills/analysis-orchestrator/reference.md` | Step 0 picks YAML or Interactive mode and adds "Resolve the Run Config". Step 1 becomes "Pre-processing" (semantic only) plus "Generate Report"; the per-CLI suffix tables and old Step 1.5 are gone. Step 2 skip keys on `comparison_method` |
| `skills/analysis-orchestrator/SKILL.md` | Trigger description covers "run it from config"; Step 0 and 1 index lines updated |

### Docs (2 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/how-to/agent.md` | New "Run the agent from a YAML config" section with the scope and config shape table; links to the wrapper's schema doc |
| `TraceLens/Agent/Analysis/README.md` | Pointer to the YAML section, `cache/run_config.yaml` and `run_config.resolved.yaml` in the output tree, and step numbers aligned with `reference.md` (Steps 0-12, including the Step 2 gate and Step 11 PNG render) |

### Evals and config (3 files)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `TraceLens/Agent/Analysis/evals/partial_tests/README.md`, `run_partial_tests.sh` | "Step 1.S" renamed to "Step 1 pre-processing" |
| `.importlinter` | Two ignore lines: the wrapper and `reporting_utils` import `Agent.Analysis.utils.arch_utils` |

### Tests (1 file)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `tests/test_analysis_agent_config_utils.py` | New. Completion per scope, `build` matches the equivalent YAML, structural rejections, `add_diff_stats`, and the CLI's printed variables and failure exits |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: 78 passed, including `tests/test_analysis_agent_config_utils.py`. `black` clean.
- [x] YAML mode end to end on six cases: training standalone, inference graph-capture standalone, deterministic fallback, comparative, comparative with graph capture, and semantic. Compute findings match the pre-PR reference reports on every case; marker and `validate_report` checks pass. One system-level finding drifted on the inference graph-capture case.
- [x] `analysis.json` `compute_optimizations` is identical to the pre-PR reports on the three standalone cases, and Hyperloom's task loader expands it without errors.
- [x] Interactive mode on the same six cases converges with YAML mode: the same resolved config, and identical perf report CSVs (the semantic case differs only in LLM label columns, with equal purity). The fallback `analysis.md` is byte-identical.
- [x] Negative cases (wrong platform, `capture_folder` on a semantic job) stop in Step 0 with the expected error.

### Sync with Main

Once #1094 is merged with main, sync changes. The per-mode report CLIs are untouched, so the old Step 1 prose works as before.
 
## Net diff (related to agent related changes ONLY)

```
10 files changed, 900 insertions(+), 147 deletions(-)
```

+"""Complete and check the run config the analysis orchestrator hands to the
+perf report wrapper.
+
+    python3 -m TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.config_utils build ...
+    python3 -m TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.config_utils check --config run.yaml
+    python3 -m TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.config_utils set-diff-stats \\
+        --config <output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml --path <output_dir>/semantic/tracediff_output/diff_stats.csv
+
+Every front end (interactive answers, a user YAML, Hyperloom) produces a dict in
+the wrapper's schema. ``check_config`` rejects a wrong shape for the scope,
+adds the wiring and forces the agent report flags on, then lets the wrapper
+validate the result. Every change is printed. The completed config is written to
+``<output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml`` only when all three phases pass. That
+file is the wrapper's input only: a re-check of it reports job 1's platform as
+platform2.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import copy
+import json
+import os
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+import yaml
+
+from TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_from_config import (
+    ConfigError,
+    load_run_config,
+    plan_reports,
+)
+
+# Constants
+SCOPES = ("standalone", "comparative", "semantic")
+_DEFAULT_FLAGS = {
+    "enable_pseudo_ops": True,
+    "group_by_num_kernels": True,
+    "include_call_stack": True,
+}
+AGENT_REPORT_FLAGS = {
+    "default": _DEFAULT_FLAGS,
+    "inference": {**_DEFAULT_FLAGS, "group_by_parent_module": True},
+}
+_PATH_KEYS = ("trace_path", "capture_folder")
+_COMPARISON_KEYS = ("compare_to", "precomputed_diff_stats")
+_EXPLICIT_KEYS = ("analysis_mode", "output_dir", "jobs")
+_CACHE_CONFIG_PATH = os.path.join("cache", "run_config.yaml")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class AnalysisConfig:
+    run_config: dict  # completed, wrapper schema, written to cache/run_config.yaml
+    changes: List[Tuple[str, str]]  # (verb, text); verb is added/set/renamed/removed
+    variables: Dict[str, str]  # the orchestrator's variables
+
+
+def check_config(config: dict, scope: Optional[str] = None) -> AnalysisConfig:
+    """Run the three phases on ``config``. Raises ``ConfigError``.
+
+    ``config`` is not modified. ``scope`` is derived when the shape makes it
+    unambiguous.
+    """
+    jobs = config.get("jobs")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(config.get("analysis_mode"), str)
+        or not isinstance(jobs, list)
+        or not jobs
+        or not all(isinstance(job, dict) for job in jobs)
+    ):
+        # The wrapper owns the message for a malformed analysis_mode or jobs
+        # list, and raises on it.
+        plan_reports(config)
+
+    if scope is None:
+        if len(jobs) == 1:
+            scope = "standalone"
+        elif len(jobs) == 2 and any(job.get("compare_to") for job in jobs):
+            scope = "comparative"
+        else:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "scope is not stated and cannot be derived from this config; "
+                "pass one of: " + ", ".join(SCOPES) + "."
+            )
+    elif scope not in SCOPES:
+        raise ConfigError(f"unknown scope {scope!r}; use one of: {', '.join(SCOPES)}.")
+
+    paths = {"output_dir": config.get("output_dir")}
+    errors = []
+    for index, job in enumerate(jobs):
+        if job.get("platform") is None:
+            errors.append(
+                f"jobs[{index}] needs a platform, not gpu_arch_json_path: "
+                "the analysis steps need a platform name."
+            )
+        for key in _PATH_KEYS:
+            paths[f"jobs[{index}].{key}"] = job.get(key)
+        compare = job.get("compare_to")
+        if isinstance(compare, dict):
+            for key in _PATH_KEYS:
+                paths[f"jobs[{index}].compare_to.{key}"] = compare.get(key)
+        paths[f"jobs[{index}].precomputed_diff_stats"] = job.get(
+            "precomputed_diff_stats"
+        )
+    errors += [
+        f"{where} must be an absolute path: {value}"
+        for where, value in paths.items()
+        if isinstance(value, str) and not os.path.isabs(value)
+    ]
+    errors += _shape_errors(scope, jobs, config.get("analysis_mode"))
+    if errors:
+        raise ConfigError("\n".join(errors))
+
+    completed = copy.deepcopy(config)
+    jobs = completed["jobs"]
+    changes = []
+    if scope == "standalone":
+        name = jobs[0].pop("name", None)
+        if name is not None:
+            changes.append(("removed", f"jobs[0].name: {name}"))
+    else:
+        for index, job in enumerate(jobs):
+            name = f"trace{index + 1}"
+            if job.get("name") is None:
+                changes.append(("added", f"jobs[{index}].name: {name}"))
+            elif job["name"] != name:
+                changes.append(
+                    ("renamed", f"jobs[{index}].name: {job['name']} -> {name}")
+                )
+            job["name"] = name
+        if scope == "comparative" and jobs[0].get("compare_to") is None:
+            jobs[0]["compare_to"] = {
+                key: jobs[1][key] for key in _PATH_KEYS if jobs[1].get(key) is not None
+            }
+            changes.append(
+                ("added", f"jobs[0].compare_to: {json.dumps(jobs[0]['compare_to'])}")
+            )
+        platform = jobs[0]["platform"]
+        platform2 = jobs[1]["platform"]
+        if platform2 != platform:
+            changes.append(
+                (
+                    "set",
+                    f"jobs[1].platform: {platform}   (was {platform2}, kept as platform2)",
+                )
+            )
+        jobs[1]["platform"] = platform
+
+    for flag, value in AGENT_REPORT_FLAGS.get(
+        completed.get("analysis_mode"), {}
+    ).items():
+        if flag not in completed:
+            changes.append(("added", f"{flag}: {json.dumps(value)}"))
+        elif completed[flag] != value:
+            changes.append(
+                (
+                    "set",
+                    f"{flag}: {json.dumps(value)}   (was {json.dumps(completed[flag])})",
+                )
+            )
+        completed[flag] = value
+
+    plans = plan_reports(completed)
+
+    variables = {
+        "comparison_scope": "standalone" if scope == "standalone" else "comparative",
+        "trace_path": plans[0].trace_path,
+        "platform": plans[0].platform,
+        "output_dir": os.path.dirname(plans[0].output_xlsx_path),
+    }
+    if scope != "standalone":
+        variables.update(
+            comparison_method="semantic" if scope == "semantic" else "tracediff",
+            trace2_path=plans[1].trace_path,
+            platform2=platform2,
+        )
+    return AnalysisConfig(completed, changes, variables)
+
+
+def add_diff_stats(config: dict, path: str) -> Tuple[dict, Tuple[str, str]]:
+    """Return ``config`` with job 1 reading ``path`` as its diff stats, and the
+    change. An existing diff stats path on job 1 is replaced. Raises
+    ``ConfigError`` unless ``config`` is semantic-shaped, ``path`` is absolute
+    and the wrapper accepts the result."""
+    updated = copy.deepcopy(config)
+    old = updated["jobs"][0].pop("precomputed_diff_stats", None)
+    errors = _shape_errors("semantic", updated["jobs"], updated.get("analysis_mode"))
+    if not os.path.isabs(path):
+        errors.append(f"path must be an absolute path: {path}")
+    if errors:
+        raise ConfigError("\n".join(errors))
+    updated["jobs"][0]["precomputed_diff_stats"] = path
+    plan_reports(updated)
+    if old in (None, path):
+        return updated, ("added", f"jobs[0].precomputed_diff_stats: {path}")
+    return updated, ("set", f"jobs[0].precomputed_diff_stats: {path}   (was {old})")
+
+
+def main(argv=None) -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Complete and check the analysis agent's run config."
+    )
+    commands = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+
+    build = commands.add_parser(
+        "build", help="Build the config from arguments, then check it."
+    )
+    build.add_argument("--scope", choices=SCOPES)
+    build.add_argument("--analysis_mode", required=True)
+    build.add_argument("--output_dir", required=True)
+    build.add_argument(
+        "--job",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        help="key=value,... for one job; repeat per job. Dotted keys nest. "
+        "Values cannot contain commas; use check with a YAML file for those.",
+    )
+    build.add_argument(
+        "--set",
+        action="append",
+        default=[],
+        help="key=value for a top-level key; dotted keys nest.",
+    )
+
+    check = commands.add_parser("check", help="Check a run YAML.")
+    check.add_argument("--config", required=True)
+    check.add_argument("--scope", choices=SCOPES)
+
+    stats = commands.add_parser(
+        "set-diff-stats", help="Point job 1 at a precomputed diff_stats.csv."
+    )
+    stats.add_argument("--config", required=True)
+    stats.add_argument("--path", required=True)
+
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        if args.command == "set-diff-stats":
+            config, change = add_diff_stats(load_run_config(args.config), args.path)
+            path, rows = args.config, [change]
+        else:
+            if args.command == "build":
+                config = {
+                    "analysis_mode": args.analysis_mode,
+                    "output_dir": args.output_dir,
+                    **_assign_pairs(args.set, _EXPLICIT_KEYS),
+                    "jobs": [_assign_pairs(job.split(",")) for job in args.job],
+                }
+            else:
+                config = load_run_config(args.config)
+            result = check_config(config, args.scope)
+            config = result.run_config
+            path = os.path.join(result.variables["output_dir"], _CACHE_CONFIG_PATH)
+            rows = [
+                *result.changes,
+                *((None, f"{key}={value}") for key, value in result.variables.items()),
+                ("wrote", path),
+            ]
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)), exist_ok=True)
+        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            yaml.safe_dump(config, handle, sort_keys=False)
+    except (ConfigError, OSError) as exc:
+        parser.error(str(exc))
+
+    for verb, text in rows:
+        print(text if verb is None else f"{verb:<8}{text}")
+
+
+def _shape_errors(
+    scope: str, jobs: List[dict], analysis_mode: Optional[str]
+) -> List[str]:
+    errors = []
+    checked = list(enumerate(jobs))
+    keys = _COMPARISON_KEYS
+    if scope == "standalone":
+        if len(jobs) != 1:
+            errors.append(f"standalone takes exactly 1 job, got {len(jobs)}.")
+    elif scope == "semantic":
+        if len(jobs) != 2:
+            errors.append(f"semantic takes exactly 2 jobs, got {len(jobs)}.")
+        if analysis_mode != "inference":
+            errors.append("semantic needs analysis_mode inference.")
+        keys += ("capture_folder",)
+    else:
+        if len(jobs) != 2:
+            return [f"comparative takes exactly 2 jobs, got {len(jobs)}."]
+        checked = [(1, jobs[1])]
+        target = {
+            key: jobs[1][key] for key in _PATH_KEYS if jobs[1].get(key) is not None
+        }
+        if jobs[0].get("compare_to") not in (None, target):
+            errors.append(
+                "comparative: jobs[0].compare_to must point at jobs[1]'s "
+                "trace_path and capture_folder."

+        f"{scope}: jobs[{index}] takes no {key}."
+        for index, job in checked
+        for key in keys
+        if job.get(key) is not None
+    ]
+
+
+def _assign_pairs(pairs: Iterable[str], reserved: Tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict:
+    target = {}
+    for pair in pairs:
+        key, separator, value = pair.partition("=")
+        parts = key.split(".")
+        if not separator or "" in parts:
+            raise ConfigError(f"expected key=value, got {pair!r}.")
+        if parts[0] in reserved:
+            raise ConfigError(f"{parts[0]} has its own argument, not --set.")
+        *parents, leaf = parts
+        node = target
+        for parent in parents:
+            node = node.setdefault(parent, {})
+            if not isinstance(node, dict):
+                raise ConfigError(f"{pair!r} nests into {parent}, already a value.")
+        try:
+            node[leaf] = yaml.safe_load(value)
+        except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
+            raise ConfigError(f"invalid YAML value in {pair!r}: {exc}") from exc
+    return target
+
+

+    main()

+
+Top-level keys other than ``analysis_mode``, ``output_dir``, and ``jobs`` must
+be parameter names of the selected report function. They apply to every job.

+flag isn't given. For ``inference`` that turns ``collective_analysis`` off.
+
+A job's ``compare_to`` behaves like ``comparison_json_path``: it adds diff
+columns and a ``diff_stats`` sheet to that job's report and writes nothing for
+the compared trace.

+one job, every job needs a ``name`` and writes ``perf_report_<name>.xlsx`` and

+back as ``run_config.resolved.yaml`` with every flag explicit and absolute
+paths. Jobs run in order, and the first failure stops the run.

+import os

+def plan_reports(config: Mapping[str, Any]) -> List[PlannedJob]:
+    """Validate ``config`` and return one plan per job. Does not open traces."""
+    if not isinstance(config, Mapping):
+        raise ConfigError("config must be a mapping.")
+
+    mode = config.get("analysis_mode")
+    if mode not in _MODES:
+        raise ConfigError(
+            "analysis_mode is required and must be one of: " + ", ".join(_MODES) + "."
+        )
+
+    output_dir = config.get("output_dir")
+    if not isinstance(output_dir, str) or not output_dir.strip():
+        raise ConfigError("output_dir is required and must be a non-empty string.")
+    output_dir = os.path.abspath(output_dir)
+
+    jobs = config.get("jobs")
+    if not isinstance(jobs, list) or not jobs:
+        raise ConfigError("jobs is required and must be a non-empty list.")
+
+    accepted = _accepted_params(_report_targets()[mode])
+    kwargs = _report_kwargs(config, accepted, _CLI_DEFAULTS[mode])
+
+    multi = len(jobs) > 1
+    names = set()
+    planned: List[PlannedJob] = []
+    for index, job in enumerate(jobs):
+        parsed = _validate_job(job, index, mode, require_name=multi)
+        name = parsed["name"]
+        if name is not None:
+            if name in names:
+                raise ConfigError(f"duplicate job name {name!r}.")
+            names.add(name)
+        stem = "perf_report" if name is None else f"perf_report_{name}"
+        planned.append(
+            PlannedJob(
+                analysis_mode=mode,
+                output_xlsx_path=os.path.join(output_dir, stem + ".xlsx"),
+                output_csvs_dir=os.path.join(output_dir, stem + "_csvs"),
+                kwargs=dict(kwargs),
+                **parsed,
+            )
+        )
+    return planned
+
+
+def run_config(
+    config: Mapping[str, Any],
+    *,
+    runners: Optional[Mapping[str, Callable]] = None,
+    merge_capture: Optional[Callable[[str, str], Any]] = None,
+) -> List[Any]:
+    """Validate, then run one report per job.
+
+    ``runners`` maps ``analysis_mode`` to a callable. The default map is the
+    real report functions. ``merge_capture(capture_folder, trace_path)`` builds
+    the inference augmented tree. Tests pass substitutes for both.
+    """
+    plans = plan_reports(config)
+    selected = dict(_report_targets() if runners is None else runners)
+    merge = _merge_capture if merge_capture is None else merge_capture
+    output_dir = os.path.dirname(plans[0].output_xlsx_path)
+    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(
+        os.path.join(output_dir, RESOLVED_CONFIG_NAME), "w", encoding="utf-8"
+    ) as handle:
+        yaml.safe_dump(_resolved_from_plans(plans), handle, sort_keys=False)
+    results = []
+    for index, plan in enumerate(plans, start=1):
+        print(
+            f"[{index}/{len(plans)}] {plan.name or 'report'}: "
+            f"{plan.trace_path} -> {plan.output_xlsx_path}"
+        )
+        if plan.analysis_mode not in selected:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"no report function registered for analysis_mode {plan.analysis_mode!r}."
+            )
+        call = dict(plan.kwargs)
+        call["profile_json_path"] = plan.trace_path
+        call["output_xlsx_path"] = plan.output_xlsx_path
+        call["output_csvs_dir"] = plan.output_csvs_dir
+        if plan.platform is not None:
+            call["gpu_arch_platform"] = plan.platform
+        else:
+            call["gpu_arch_json_path"] = plan.gpu_arch_json_path
+        if plan.capture_folder is not None:
+            call["augmented_tree"] = merge(plan.capture_folder, plan.trace_path)
+        if plan.compare_trace_path is not None:
+            call["comparison_json_path"] = plan.compare_trace_path
+        if plan.compare_capture_folder is not None:
+            call["comparison_augmented_tree"] = merge(
+                plan.compare_capture_folder, plan.compare_trace_path
+            )
+        if plan.precomputed_diff_stats is not None:
+            call["precomputed_diff_stats"] = plan.precomputed_diff_stats
+        results.append(selected[plan.analysis_mode](**call))
+    return results
+
+
+def resolve_config(config: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict:
+    """Return ``config`` as a runnable YAML dict with every report flag explicit.
+
+    Paths are absolute. This is what ``run_config`` writes to
+    ``<output_dir>/run_config.resolved.yaml`` before the first job runs.
+    """
+    return _resolved_from_plans(plan_reports(config))
+
+
+def _resolved_from_plans(plans: List[PlannedJob]) -> dict:
+    mode = plans[0].analysis_mode
+    params = inspect.signature(_report_targets()[mode]).parameters
+    flags = {
+        name: plans[0].kwargs.get(name, params[name].default)
+        for name in _accepted_params(_report_targets()[mode])
+        if name not in _WRAPPER_KWARGS
+    }
+    jobs = []
+    for plan in plans:
+        job = {}
+        if plan.name is not None:
+            job["name"] = plan.name
+        job["trace_path"] = plan.trace_path
+        if plan.platform is not None:
+            job["platform"] = plan.platform
+        else:
+            job["gpu_arch_json_path"] = plan.gpu_arch_json_path
+        if plan.capture_folder is not None:
+            job["capture_folder"] = plan.capture_folder
+        if plan.compare_trace_path is not None:
+            job["compare_to"] = {"trace_path": plan.compare_trace_path}
+            if plan.compare_capture_folder is not None:
+                job["compare_to"]["capture_folder"] = plan.compare_capture_folder
+        if plan.precomputed_diff_stats is not None:
+            job["precomputed_diff_stats"] = plan.precomputed_diff_stats
+        jobs.append(job)
+    return {
+        "analysis_mode": mode,
+        "output_dir": os.path.dirname(plans[0].output_xlsx_path),
+        **flags,
+        "jobs": jobs,
+    }
+
+
+def run_config_file(path: str, **kwargs) -> List[Any]:
+    """Load ``path`` and run it."""
+    return run_config(load_run_config(path), **kwargs)
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description="Generate TraceLens perf reports from a YAML run config."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--config",
+        required=True,
+        help="Path to the run YAML (analysis_mode, output_dir, jobs).",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        run_config_file(args.config)
+    except ConfigError as exc:
+        parser.error(str(exc))
+
+
+def _report_targets() -> Dict[str, Callable]:
+    from TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_pytorch import (
+        generate_perf_report_pytorch as training_report,
+    )
+    from TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_pytorch_inference import (
+        generate_perf_report_pytorch as inference_report,
+    )

+
+
+def _accepted_params(fn: Callable) -> set:
+    params = inspect.signature(fn).parameters
+    return {
+        name
+        for name, param in params.items()
+        if param.kind
+        in (
+            inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
+            inspect.Parameter.KEYWORD_ONLY,
+        )
+    }
+
+
+def _report_kwargs(
+    config: Mapping[str, Any], accepted: set, cli_defaults: Mapping[str, Any]
+) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    wrapper = sorted(set(config) & _WRAPPER_KWARGS)
+    unknown = sorted(set(config) - _CONFIG_KEYS - _WRAPPER_KWARGS - accepted)
+    if wrapper or unknown:
+        details = []
+        if wrapper:
+            details.append(
+                "keys that belong on a job or are set by the wrapper: "
+                + ", ".join(wrapper)
+            )
+        if unknown:
+            details.append(
+                "unknown keys (not config fields or report parameters): "
+                + ", ".join(unknown)
+            )
+        raise ConfigError("; ".join(details) + ".")
+
+    kwargs = {key: config[key] for key in config if key in accepted}
+    for key, value in cli_defaults.items():
+        if key in accepted and key not in kwargs:
+            kwargs[key] = value
+    return kwargs
+
+
+def _validate_job(job: Any, index: int, mode: str, *, require_name: bool) -> dict:
+    where = f"jobs[{index}]"
+    if not isinstance(job, dict):
+        raise ConfigError(f"{where} must be a mapping.")
+    extra = sorted(set(job) - _JOB_KEYS)
+    if extra:
+        raise ConfigError(
+            f"{where} has unknown keys: " + ", ".join(extra) + ". "
+            "Report flags belong at the top level."
+        )
+
+    name = job.get("name")
+    if name is None:
+        if require_name:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"{where}.name is required when there is more than one job."
+            )
+    elif (
+        not isinstance(name, str)
+        or not name
+        or any(ch not in _NAME_CHARS for ch in name)
+    ):
+        raise ConfigError(
+            f"{where}.name must contain only letters, digits, '_', '-' or '.'."
+        )
+
+    trace_path = _existing_file(job.get("trace_path"), f"{where}.trace_path")
+
+    platform = job.get("platform")
+    arch_path = job.get("gpu_arch_json_path")
+    if (platform is None) == (arch_path is None):
+        raise ConfigError(
+            f"{where} needs exactly one of platform or gpu_arch_json_path."
+        )
+    if platform is not None:
+        known = list_platforms()
+        if platform not in known:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"{where}.platform {platform!r} is not a known arch "
+                f"({', '.join(known)}). Use gpu_arch_json_path or TL_EXTENSION."
+            )
+    else:
+        arch_path = _existing_file(arch_path, f"{where}.gpu_arch_json_path")
+
+    capture_folder = _optional_dir(job.get("capture_folder"), f"{where}.capture_folder")
+    if capture_folder is not None and mode != "inference":
+        raise ConfigError(
+            f"{where}.capture_folder is only valid for analysis_mode inference."
+        )
+
+    compare_trace = None
+    compare_capture = None
+    compare = job.get("compare_to")
+    if compare is not None:
+        if not isinstance(compare, dict):
+            raise ConfigError(f"{where}.compare_to must be a mapping.")
+        extra = sorted(set(compare) - _COMPARE_KEYS)
+        if extra:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"{where}.compare_to has unknown keys: " + ", ".join(extra) + "."
+            )
+        compare_trace = _existing_file(
+            compare.get("trace_path"), f"{where}.compare_to.trace_path"
+        )
+        compare_capture = _optional_dir(
+            compare.get("capture_folder"), f"{where}.compare_to.capture_folder"
+        )
+        if compare_capture is not None and mode != "inference":
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"{where}.compare_to.capture_folder is only valid for analysis_mode inference."
+            )
+
+    diff_stats = job.get("precomputed_diff_stats")
+    if diff_stats is not None:
+        if compare is not None:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                f"{where} cannot set both compare_to and precomputed_diff_stats."
+            )
+        diff_stats = _existing_file(diff_stats, f"{where}.precomputed_diff_stats")
+
+    return {
+        "name": name,
+        "trace_path": trace_path,
+        "platform": platform,
+        "gpu_arch_json_path": arch_path,
+        "capture_folder": capture_folder,
+        "compare_trace_path": compare_trace,
+        "compare_capture_folder": compare_capture,
+        "precomputed_diff_stats": diff_stats,
+    }
+
+
+def _existing_file(value: Any, where: str) -> str:
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
+        raise ConfigError(f"{where} is required and must be a string.")
+    if not os.path.isfile(value):
+        raise ConfigError(f"{where} not found: {value}")
+    return os.path.abspath(value)
+
+
+def _optional_dir(value: Any, where: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
+        raise ConfigError(f"{where} must be a non-empty string.")
+    if not os.path.isdir(value):
+        raise ConfigError(f"{where} not found: {value}")
+    return os.path.abspath(value)
+
+
+def _merge_capture(capture_folder: str, trace_path: str):
+    from TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_pytorch_inference import (

+        capture_folder, metadata_json_path, trace_path
+    )

+# Generate TraceLens performance reports from a YAML config
+```{meta}
+:description: Learn how to describe a TraceLens performance-report run in one YAML file covering training, inference, graph capture, prefill and decode, and trace comparison.
+:keywords: TraceLens, YAML, run config, performance report, PyTorch profiler, inference, vLLM, SGLang, graph capture, speculative decoding, prefill, decode, TraceDiff, ROCm
+```
+
+This topic shows how to run TraceLens performance reports from a single YAML
+file. It's the recommended way to generate PyTorch reports: one command covers
+training and inference traces, and the file records exactly which options were
+used. `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch` and
+`TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch_inference` keep working unchanged.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Before running a config, confirm you have the following:
+
+- [TraceLens installed](../install/install.md).
+- One or more `torch.profiler` traces (`.json` or `.json.gz`).
+- For graph-mode inference, the graph-capture folder for each trace. See
+  [Generate a PyTorch inference performance report](./generate-perf-report-pytorch-inference.md).
+
+## Run a config
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config --config run.yaml
+```
+
+The same entry point is available as
+`python -m TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_from_config --config run.yaml`.
+
+The whole file is checked before any trace is opened, so a typo in the last job
+fails in seconds instead of after the first report finishes.
+
+## Write a config
+
+A config has three required keys and a list of jobs. Each job produces one
+report.
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/llama_train/trace.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Top-level keys
+
+| Key | Required | Description |
+|-----|----------|-------------|
+| `analysis_mode` | yes | `default` for training and plain PyTorch traces. `inference` for vLLM, SGLang, ATOM, and xDiT traces, with or without graph capture. |
+| `output_dir` | yes | Directory for the reports. |
+| `jobs` | yes | List of jobs. See the job keys below. |
+| any report option | no | Any parameter of the selected report function, by its Python name (for example `kernel_summary: true`, `topk_ops: 50`). Applies to every job. |
+
+### Job keys
+
+| Key | Required | Description |
+|-----|----------|-------------|
+| `name` | when there's more than one job | Used in the output file names. Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, and `.`. |
+| `trace_path` | yes | Trace to analyze. |
+| `platform` | one of the two | Bundled or `TL_EXTENSION` architecture name, for example `MI300X`. |
+| `gpu_arch_json_path` | one of the two | Path to an architecture JSON file, for hardware that isn't bundled. |
+| `capture_folder` | no | Graph-capture folder. `inference` only. |
+| `compare_to` | no | `trace_path` of a second trace, plus `capture_folder` in `inference`. Same as `--comparison_json_path`. |
+| `precomputed_diff_stats` | no | A `diff_stats.csv` to use instead of running TraceDiff. Can't be combined with `compare_to`. |
+
+Report options go at the top level, not on a job. Each job can use a different
+architecture, so one config can cover traces from different GPUs.
+
+## Defaults
+
+An option the config doesn't set has the same default as in the matching CLI,
+so a config with no options produces the same report as the CLI with no flags.
+For example, `collective_analysis` is on in `default` and off in `inference`.
+
+To get the same report as the TraceLens Agent, set these options:
+
+```yaml
+enable_pseudo_ops: true
+group_by_num_kernels: true
+include_call_stack: true
+group_by_parent_module: true   # inference only
+```
+
+## Outputs
+
+| Jobs | Files in `output_dir` |
+|------|-----------------------|
+| One, without `name` | `perf_report.xlsx`, `perf_report_csvs/` |
+| Any job with `name` | `perf_report_<name>.xlsx`, `perf_report_<name>_csvs/` |
+
+Before the first job runs, TraceLens writes `run_config.resolved.yaml` to
+`output_dir`. It's the same config with every report option spelled out and
+every path absolute, so you can check later which options produced a report,
+or rerun it as is.
+
+Jobs run in the order listed. If a job fails, the run stops with a non-zero
+exit code and the reports already written are kept. Relative paths are resolved
+against the directory you run the command from, as in the CLIs.
+
+## Examples
+
+### Change report options
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output
+include_call_stack: true
+kernel_summary: true
+topk_ops: 50
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/llama_train/trace.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Inference, eager mode
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/qwen_vllm/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/qwen_vllm/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Inference with graph capture
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/qwen_vllm/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/qwen_vllm/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/qwen_vllm/capture_traces
+```
+
+Speculative decoding uses the same config. The drafter and target graphs are
+in the same capture folder.
+
+### Prefill and decode
+
+Prefill and decode are two inference jobs, each with its own trace and capture
+folder:
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/dsv2lite_pd/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - name: prefill_rank0
+    trace_path: /data/dsv2lite_pd/prefill/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/dsv2lite_pd/prefill/capture_traces
+  - name: decode_rank0
+    trace_path: /data/dsv2lite_pd/decode/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/dsv2lite_pd/decode/capture_traces
+```
+
+### Compare two traces
+
+`compare_to` adds speedup, delta, and lowest common ancestor (LCA) columns to
+the job's `unified_perf_summary`, plus a `diff_stats` sheet. It doesn't write a
+report for the compared trace. Add a second job if you want one:
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/ab/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - name: new
+    trace_path: /data/ab/new.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/ab/new_capture
+    compare_to:
+      trace_path: /data/ab/old.json.gz
+      capture_folder: /data/ab/old_capture
+  - name: old
+    trace_path: /data/ab/old.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/ab/old_capture
+```
+
+### Hardware that isn't bundled
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/llama_train/trace.json.gz
+    gpu_arch_json_path: /data/arch/my_gpu.json
+```

+"""Complete and check the run config the analysis orchestrator hands to the
+perf report wrapper.
+
+    python3 -m TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.config_utils build ...
+    python3 -m TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.config_utils check --config run.yaml
+    python3 -m TraceLens.Agent.Analysis.utils.config_utils set-diff-stats \\
+        --config <output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml --path <output_dir>/semantic/tracediff_output/diff_stats.csv
+
+Every front end (interactive answers, a user YAML, Hyperloom) produces a dict in
+the wrapper's schema. ``check_config`` rejects a wrong shape for the scope,
+adds the wiring and forces the agent report flags on, then lets the wrapper
+validate the result. Every change is printed. The completed config is written to
+``<output_dir>/cache/run_config.yaml`` only when all three phases pass. That
+file is the wrapper's input only: a re-check of it reports job 1's platform as
+platform2.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import copy
+import json
+import os
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+import yaml
+
+from TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_from_config import (
+    ConfigError,
+    load_run_config,
+    plan_reports,
+)
+
+# Constants
+SCOPES = ("standalone", "comparative", "semantic")
+_DEFAULT_FLAGS = {
+    "enable_pseudo_ops": True,
+    "group_by_num_kernels": True,
+    "include_call_stack": True,
+}
+AGENT_REPORT_FLAGS = {
+    "default": _DEFAULT_FLAGS,
+    "inference": {**_DEFAULT_FLAGS, "group_by_parent_module": True},
+}
+_PATH_KEYS = ("trace_path", "capture_folder")
+_COMPARISON_KEYS = ("compare_to", "precomputed_diff_stats")
+_EXPLICIT_KEYS = ("analysis_mode", "output_dir", "jobs")
+_CACHE_CONFIG_PATH = os.path.join("cache", "run_config.yaml")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class AnalysisConfig:
+    run_config: dict  # completed, wrapper schema, written to cache/run_config.yaml
+    changes: List[Tuple[str, str]]  # (verb, text); verb is added/set/renamed/removed
+    variables: Dict[str, str]  # the orchestrator's variables
+
+
+def check_config(config: dict, scope: Optional[str] = None) -> AnalysisConfig:
+    """Run the three phases on ``config``. Raises ``ConfigError``.
+
+    ``config`` is not modified. ``scope`` is derived when the shape makes it
+    unambiguous.
+    """
+    jobs = config.get("jobs")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(config.get("analysis_mode"), str)
+        or not isinstance(jobs, list)
+        or not jobs
+        or not all(isinstance(job, dict) for job in jobs)
+    ):
+        # The wrapper owns the message for a malformed analysis_mode or jobs
+        # list, and raises on it.
+        plan_reports(config)
+
+    if scope is None:
+        if len(jobs) == 1:
+            scope = "standalone"
+        elif len(jobs) == 2 and any(job.get("compare_to") for job in jobs):
+            scope = "comparative"
+        else:
+            raise ConfigError(
+                "scope is not stated and cannot be derived from this config; "
+                "pass one of: " + ", ".join(SCOPES) + "."
+            )

+# Generate TraceLens performance reports from a YAML config

+
+This topic shows how to run TraceLens performance reports from a single YAML
+file. It's the recommended way to generate PyTorch reports: one command covers
+training and inference traces, and the file records exactly which options were
+used. `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch` and
+`TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch_inference` keep working unchanged.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Before running a config, confirm you have the following:
+
+- [TraceLens installed](../install/install.md).
+- One or more `torch.profiler` traces (`.json` or `.json.gz`).
+- For graph-mode inference, the graph-capture folder for each trace. See
+  [Generate a PyTorch inference performance report](./generate-perf-report-pytorch-inference.md).
+
+## Run a config
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config --config run.yaml
+```
+
+The same entry point is available as
+`python -m TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_from_config --config run.yaml`.
+
+The whole file is checked before any trace is opened, so a typo in the last job
+fails in seconds instead of after the first report finishes.
+
+## Write a config
+
+A config has three required keys and a list of jobs. Each job produces one
+report.
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/llama_train/trace.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Top-level keys
+
+| Key | Required | Description |
+|-----|----------|-------------|
+| `analysis_mode` | yes | `default` for training and plain PyTorch traces. `inference` for vLLM, SGLang, ATOM, and xDiT traces, with or without graph capture. |
+| `output_dir` | yes | Directory for the reports. |
+| `jobs` | yes | List of jobs. See the job keys below. |
+| any report option | no | Any parameter of the selected report function, by its Python name (for example `kernel_summary: true`, `topk_ops: 50`). Applies to every job. |
+
+### Job keys
+
+| Key | Required | Description |
+|-----|----------|-------------|
+| `name` | when there's more than one job | Used in the output file names. Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, and `.`. |
+| `trace_path` | yes | Trace to analyze. |
+| `platform` | one of the two | Bundled or `TL_EXTENSION` architecture name, for example `MI300X`. |
+| `gpu_arch_json_path` | one of the two | Path to an architecture JSON file, for hardware that isn't bundled. |
+| `capture_folder` | no | Graph-capture folder. `inference` only. |
+| `compare_to` | no | `trace_path` of a second trace, plus `capture_folder` in `inference`. Same as `--comparison_json_path`. |
+| `precomputed_diff_stats` | no | A `diff_stats.csv` to use instead of running TraceDiff. Can't be combined with `compare_to`. |
+
+Report options go at the top level, not on a job. Each job can use a different
+architecture, so one config can cover traces from different GPUs.
+
+## Defaults
+
+An option the config doesn't set has the same default as in the matching CLI,
+so a config with no options produces the same report as the CLI with no flags.
+For example, `collective_analysis` is on in `default` and off in `inference`.
+
+To get the same report as the TraceLens Agent, set these options:
+
+```yaml
+enable_pseudo_ops: true
+group_by_num_kernels: true
+include_call_stack: true
+group_by_parent_module: true   # inference only
+```
+
+## Outputs
+
+| Jobs | Files in `output_dir` |
+|------|-----------------------|
+| One, without `name` | `perf_report.xlsx`, `perf_report_csvs/` |
+| Any job with `name` | `perf_report_<name>.xlsx`, `perf_report_<name>_csvs/` |

+Before the first job runs, TraceLens writes `run_config.resolved.yaml` to
+`output_dir`. It's the same config with every report option spelled out and
+every path absolute, so you can check later which options produced a report,
+or rerun it as is.
+
+Jobs run in the order listed. If a job fails, the run stops with a non-zero
+exit code and the reports already written are kept. Relative paths are resolved
+against the directory you run the command from, as in the CLIs.

+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output

+# Generate TraceLens performance reports from a YAML config
+```{meta}
+:description: Learn how to describe a TraceLens performance-report run in one YAML file covering training, inference, graph capture, prefill and decode, and trace comparison.
+:keywords: TraceLens, YAML, run config, performance report, PyTorch profiler, inference, vLLM, SGLang, graph capture, speculative decoding, prefill, decode, TraceDiff, ROCm
+```
+
+This topic shows how to run TraceLens performance reports from a single YAML
+file. It's the recommended way to generate PyTorch reports: one command covers
+training and inference traces, and the file records exactly which options were
+used. `TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch` and
+`TraceLens_generate_perf_report_pytorch_inference` keep working unchanged.
+
+## Before you begin
+
+Before running a config, confirm you have the following:
+
+- [TraceLens installed](../install/install.md).
+- One or more `torch.profiler` traces (`.json` or `.json.gz`).
+- For graph-mode inference, the graph-capture folder for each trace. See
+  [Generate a PyTorch inference performance report](./generate-perf-report-pytorch-inference.md).
+
+## Run a config
+
+```bash
+TraceLens_generate_perf_report_from_config --config run.yaml
+```
+
+The same entry point is available as
+`python -m TraceLens.Reporting.generate_perf_report_from_config --config run.yaml`.
+
+The whole file is checked before any trace is opened, so a typo in the last job
+fails in seconds instead of after the first report finishes.
+
+## Write a config
+
+A config has three required keys and a list of jobs. Each job produces one
+report.
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/llama_train/trace.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Top-level keys
+
+| Key | Required | Description |
+|-----|----------|-------------|
+| `analysis_mode` | yes | `default` for training and plain PyTorch traces. `inference` for vLLM, SGLang, ATOM, and xDiT traces, with or without graph capture. |
+| `output_dir` | yes | Directory for the reports. |
+| `jobs` | yes | List of jobs. See the job keys below. |
+| any report option | no | Any parameter of the selected report function, by its Python name (for example `kernel_summary: true`, `topk_ops: 50`). Applies to every job. |
+
+### Job keys
+
+| Key | Required | Description |
+|-----|----------|-------------|
+| `name` | when there's more than one job | Used in the output file names. Letters, digits, `_`, `-`, and `.`. |
+| `trace_path` | yes | Trace to analyze. |
+| `platform` | one of the two | Bundled or `TL_EXTENSION` architecture name, for example `MI300X`. |
+| `gpu_arch_json_path` | one of the two | Path to an architecture JSON file, for hardware that isn't bundled. |
+| `capture_folder` | no | Graph-capture folder. `inference` only. |
+| `compare_to` | no | `trace_path` of a second trace, plus `capture_folder` in `inference`. Same as `--comparison_json_path`. |
+| `precomputed_diff_stats` | no | A `diff_stats.csv` to use instead of running TraceDiff. Can't be combined with `compare_to`. |
+
+Report options go at the top level, not on a job. Each job can use a different
+architecture, so one config can cover traces from different GPUs.
+
+## Defaults
+
+An option the config doesn't set has the same default as in the matching CLI,
+so a config with no options produces the same report as the CLI with no flags.
+For example, `collective_analysis` is on in `default` and off in `inference`.
+
+To get the same report as the TraceLens Agent, set these options:
+
+```yaml
+enable_pseudo_ops: true
+group_by_num_kernels: true
+include_call_stack: true
+group_by_parent_module: true   # inference only
+```
+
+## Outputs
+
+| Jobs | Files in `output_dir` |
+|------|-----------------------|
+| One, without `name` | `perf_report.xlsx`, `perf_report_csvs/` |
+| Any job with `name` | `perf_report_<name>.xlsx`, `perf_report_<name>_csvs/` |
+
+Before the first job runs, TraceLens writes `run_config.resolved.yaml` to
+`output_dir`. It's the same config with every report option spelled out and
+every path absolute, so you can check later which options produced a report,
+or rerun it as is.
+
+Jobs run in the order listed. If a job fails, the run stops with a non-zero
+exit code and the reports already written are kept. Relative paths are resolved
+against the directory you run the command from, as in the CLIs.
+
+## Examples
+
+### Change report options
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: default
+output_dir: /data/llama_train/analysis_output
+include_call_stack: true
+kernel_summary: true
+topk_ops: 50
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/llama_train/trace.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Inference, eager mode
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/qwen_vllm/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/qwen_vllm/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+```
+
+### Inference with graph capture
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/qwen_vllm/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - trace_path: /data/qwen_vllm/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/qwen_vllm/capture_traces
+```
+
+Speculative decoding uses the same config. The drafter and target graphs are
+in the same capture folder.
+
+### Prefill and decode
+
+Prefill and decode are two inference jobs, each with its own trace and capture
+folder:
+
+```yaml
+analysis_mode: inference
+output_dir: /data/dsv2lite_pd/analysis_output
+jobs:
+  - name: prefill_rank0
+    trace_path: /data/dsv2lite_pd/prefill/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/dsv2lite_pd/prefill/capture_traces

+    trace_path: /data/dsv2lite_pd/decode/rank0.json.gz
+    platform: MI300X
+    capture_folder: /data/dsv2lite_pd/decode/capture_traces
+```
